quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and be careful.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Stop and wait for the intersection to be clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Check only your left side mirror.
Look over your shoulder to the left or right.
Check only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder to the left or right.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors cannot show everything. You must look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If you have a blowout, take your foot off the gas and slow down gradually. Do not brake hard until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop and watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at things.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at things in a construction zone. This causes traffic congestion. Pass through carefully without stopping to watch.

questions.question: Why is it important to look far ahead when driving on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with traffic.
It helps you avoid sudden braking or turning.
It helps you see police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking far ahead helps you see problems before they happen. You can then slow down or change lanes smoothly. This keeps you safe, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Drive faster to keep your spot.
Stay in your lane no matter what.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, you should make room for merging vehicles to enter your lane.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Move completely off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down, move it completely off the road with all four wheels off the traveled part of the highway if you can.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both reasons above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both reasons above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch for them near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. They may suddenly ride from the sidewalk into the road.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Check your mirror and look over your shoulder to see if it is safe.
Check your rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirror and look over your shoulder to see if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in your blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: When are collisions most likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at about the same speed.
When one lane travels faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen when one driver moves faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Driving faster than traffic increases collision risk. Driving slower than traffic is also dangerous because it can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane closest to the direction you want to turn, then move into the first legal lane. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Stop.
Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about special conditions or hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian, but an oncoming vehicle is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then you can pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon. Merge left.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon. Merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that lanes ahead are being reduced and traffic must merge left.

questions.question: What do drivers need to do on the interstate?

options.text: Be able to safely drive at high speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires drivers to stay alert and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean passing is not allowed in either direction.

questions.question: Who do drivers turning left have to yield to?

options.text: Vehicles passing you.
Oncoming vehicles.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight. Turn only when you can do so safely without affecting oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when following a motorcycle?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow at least three to four seconds of following distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop quickly, and following too closely is dangerous for you and the rider. If the rider falls, you need extra distance to avoid them. The risk of falling is greatest on wet and icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve with no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and road markings allow it, and only if you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: What is the main idea behind defensive driving?

options.text: Other drivers will always do the right thing.
You think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
You expect nothing from others and give nothing back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means watching for mistakes other drivers might make. Be ready to react and protect yourself from their errors.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm your judgment and coordination. Even small amounts can make it harder to drive safely. Driving under the influence can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car rolls away from traffic. When parking uphill with a curb, turn toward the center so your car rolls into the curb instead.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Match the freeway traffic speed when you merge. Go at or near the speed of other cars, unless traffic is going faster than the legal limit.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect unexpected changes and dangers.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect unexpected changes and dangers.
questions.explanation: Construction zones can have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.
